result.rationale: The trajectory shows a clear pattern where the rescue team's specialists are repeatedly blocked and degraded by hostile and environmental pressure before they can reach the useful affordance (rescuing civilians). Engineer Imani is repeatedly attacked by Raider Holt's scatter-blast (turns 2 and 3, taking 29 and 25 damage), and both Imani and Security Chen take 10 damage per turn from the reactor environment once they enter reactor-entry/reactor-console zones (turns 2-5). Medic Reyes is also attacked by Raider Holt (turn 1, 21 damage) and then contested on target_zone_capacity_lost when trying to move with the escorted civilian Sato (turn 4). The reactor-heat climbs monotonically 62→100 and the reactor-instability hazard damages anyone in the reactor room, while the team's split formation leaves specialists exposed. The core bottleneck is that health/position/capacity/hostile pressure (Raider Holt's overwatch, reactor hazard, zone capacity) blocks the actors before the rescue affordance becomes actionable — Imani is at 26 health by turn 6, and the rescue objective remains at 0/2. This is survival-spatial-pressure rather than an information bottleneck (information was gained early via orbital-scan) or a local-policy-choice (the actors are attempting the correct rescue actions but are physically blocked).
